articleTitle: V2G and G2V Using Interleaved Converter for a Single-Phase Onboard Bidirectional Charger
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents the design and control of an interleaved buck-boost bidirectional converter for a non-isolated onboard battery charger used in an electric vehicle. The topology of the charger consists of two part: 1) an AC-DC inverter and 2) a DC-DC buck-boost converter. A bidirectional ac-dc converter will work in two modes, rectifying mode for G2V and inverter mode for V2G. The proposed topology of the charger is not only having bidirectional power flow capability but also providing power quality control to the utility grid. The beauty of this is concept is that the vehicle’s battery is not negative impacted while reactive power operation as the energy of the battery is not taken. Emphasized in this paper, a DC-DC converter work in two modes: buck mode for charging the battery and boost mode for discharging the battery power and injecting this power to the grid by the mean of the single-phase inverter. For G2V operation, the bidirectional dc-dc converter is controlled to work in a buck mode to bring down the voltage of the dc-link and to charge on the battery with either a current constant or voltage constant depending on battery’s SoC. In the boost mode-V2G, the converter is working in a boost mode to step up the voltage of the battery and discharge the energy into the dc-link by using interleaved boost converter with 180° phase shift for reducing the current ripple and the inductor size. The bidirectional buck-boost converter has been engineered and its control has been verified through PSIM. The simulation results have shown that the proposed converter and its control work perfectly for the G2V application.

articleTitle: New Blockchain Adoptation For Automotive Security by Using Systematic Innovation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper deals with the security matters in automotive by using the Blockchain technology and an innovative thinking skill which has been applied to develop the new prototype design from the initial idea. The Blockchain Governance Game and Fog Computing are adopted to build the new highly secure decentralized service architecture. These relatively new technologies make possible to design the Blockchain based on the automotive security. Although the paper is condensed and does not contain the details, it will be the good guideline for the direction of future research. The thinking skill called Systematic Innovation is the core to solve this problems in the proper Blockchain security network design and well demonstrated in this paper.

articleTitle: Autonomous Vehicle Security: Conceptual Model
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Nowadays, we see vehicles with different automation levels; from zero automation to fully automation vehicles. Leading car manufacturers such as Audi, Volkswagen, TESLA along with Google are becoming the lead in autonomous vehicles industry. Autonomous vehicles can have over 100 million lines of code in their modules with large number of messages being exchanged among vehicles. These vehicles have multiple connection points to the Internet. Bad code, misconfiguration and Internet exposure makes these vehicles vulnerable to different kind of malicious attacks. This paper presents a conceptual autonomous vehicle model to better understand the attack surface on autonomous vehicles. In addition, it presents real life scenarios of successful attacks on different models of vehicles. This paper introduces a conceptual model for autonomous vehicles as initial work for threat modeling of autonomous vehicles. In addition, it highlights some of the cyber security attacks on autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: The Expansion of Electrical Generations by using Capacity Market Planning in Mongolia
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents possibilities to implement a capacity market in the Mongolian energy system and analyses long term planning with different plants. Covering rapid increasing electric demand requires a complex solution in the energy system, which should support not only for the customer and stakeholders. Proposed capacity market model for energy system in Mongolia, considering existing and new entrants of generation plants.

articleTitle: Grid impact analysis of electric vehicles charging with different load profiles
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: With the seriousness of environmental problems, people begin to use electric vehicles(EVs) instead of traditional vehicles, which can reduce carbon dioxide emissions. But a large number of electric vehicles plug-in grid will arise overload, voltage deviation issue, harmonic distortion, etc. which affect the regular operation of the power grid. Seriously, it may cause blackouts in the entire power grid. Therefore, it is essential for real-time detection of grid operation safety. In this paper, we propose a sensitivity analysis of active power and voltage at the same time to identify the impact of electric vehicle charging on the different load profile. The simulation results strongly suggest that when the EV penetration rate at a specific value, it will increase the deviation of active power and voltage and influence the electricity utilisation by users. Based on these results, we can specifically recommend them about the management of charging strategic of EVs.

articleTitle: Computing Focus Time of Paragraph Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Time is a main part of any text that shows value of the document. We have two type of documents that are temporal and atemporal characters. In this paper we explain problem of focus time in historical documents using convolutional neural network (CNN) which shows the time period of text contents and it measure out the document creation time. We used to different type of documents that one is Wikipedia documents and another is web news texts. We evaluate the advantages of our method on various text documents that related to historical events in defined timelines. We used different methods for evaluating focus time of paragraph. To find the relationship between words in document we used different simulation methods and word 2vec system to get more detail results of words. Our proposed approach contains focus time of paragraphs in text documents using deep learning process.

articleTitle: Dynamic Threshold Adjustment Strategy of Supercapacitor Energy Storage System based on No-load Voltage Identification in Urban Rail Transit
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The stationary supercapacitor energy storage systems (SCESS) in urban rail transit systems can effectively recover the regenerative braking energy of the trains and reduce the fluctuation of the traction network voltage. Generally, the charge/discharge states of SCESS is determined by the voltage of the traction network; however, in actual operation, the fluctuation of the no-load voltage of the substation may result in unexpected working states of SCESS, such as barely charge/discharge. Therefore, a dynamic threshold adjustment strategy based on no-load voltage identification is proposed in this paper: the output characteristic equation of substation is fitted in real-time with the recorded substation currents and voltages, and the present value of no-load voltage is predicted by the neural network, based on which the charge and discharge thresholds of the SCESS are adjusted dynamically. Through the proposed identification method, the variation trend of the no-load voltage of Liyuan Substation in Beijing Metro Batong Line in the whole day is analyzed. Besides, simulation results show that with the proposed dynamic threshold adjustment strategy, the SCESS is charged and discharged more effectively, and the energy saving effect is significantly improved.

articleTitle: A Study on ZCS Problem Due to Phase Change in Inductive Power Transfer Charging System Applying GaN FET
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the problem that occurs when the Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS) is changed to Zero Current Switching (ZCS) in a wireless power transfer system where the position of the receiving coil changes frequently. Based on this analysis, the problem caused by the ZVS to ZCS transition is demonstrated by a detailed theoretical analysis that can be solved by using a GaN FET with wide bandgap characteristics instead of the conventional MOSFET. To verify the theory, a 500W IPT prototype with SP compensation circuitry was built. And compare the operation of ZVS and ZCS when MOSFET and GaN FET are applied. In addition, if the GaN FET is applied to the field where the resonance frequency can be changed in the wireless power transfer system, the possibility of solving the problem in the ZCS operation can be confirmed.

articleTitle: Optimized Energy Management Strategy Based on SQP Algorithm for PEMFC Hybrid Locomotive
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This study aims at improving the efficiency, durability, and performance of the hybrid system, thus an optimal energy management strategy (EMS) based on sequential quadratic programming (SQP) algorithm has been proposed. The SQP algorithm is utilized to ensure that the fuel cell work in the high efficiency range as much as possible, and that the battery SOC fluctuation is within the limited range. A test platform which is composed of battery, bidirectional DC/DC converter, fuel cell stack, unidirectional DC/DC converter, etc. has been built to verify the validity of the proposed EMS. The experimental results show that the proposed optimized EMS performs better than equivalent hydrogen consumption minimization strategy (ECMS).

articleTitle: A Neutral-Point Potential Balancing Method for a Three-Level Neutral-Point-Clamped Back-to-Back Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, a neutral-point (NP) potential balancing method based on zero-sequence voltage injection is presented for the traditional three-level neutral-point-clamped (NPC) back-to-back converter. In the control algorithm, make the NP current on the rectifier side follow the reference NP current to adjust the NP potential balancing. The relationship between NP average current and zero-sequence voltage is analyzed in theory. On this basis, choosing several key zero-sequence voltages can reduce the complexity of calculation, and one of the three phases switches will keep unchanged during each switching period, thus the switching loss is reduced, and the NP potential balancing method is optimized. The simulation results show that the optimized zero-sequence voltage injection method can suppress the NP potential fluctuation well, and has little influence on the input current harmonics.

articleTitle: A design methodology of bidirectional LLC resonant converter for energy storage systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: A design methodology of bidirectional LLC resonant converter for energy storage application is proposed. Along with the design methodology, a study on LLC resonant converter with unsymmetrical characteristics in forward and backward mode is presented. Further, a comparative study is also carried out between symmetrical and unsymmetrical bidirectional LLC resonant converter.

articleTitle: Optimal scheduling of critical peak pricing considering photovoltaic generation and electric vehicle load
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper proposes Load Serving Entities (LSEs) model that purchases energy in the wholesale market by optimally operating Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) considering Electric Vehicle (EV) load and photovoltaic (PV) generation. In the proposed scheme, LSEs determine critical event schedule and hourly bidding schedule of band capacity in power exchange for frequency control (PXFC) market. In addition, imbalance penalties due to various uncertain parameters are involved in the stochastic optimization problem with Monte Carlo scenarios. This problem is formulated as mixed integer nonlinear program (MINLP). In the simulation section, the optimal critical event schedule described in this paper is numerically verified. Also we show the profit of LSEs is affected by level of uncertain parameters. This result provides intuition that several factors should be considered in the critical peak event operating strategy of LSEs not only market conditions but also characteristics of demands and uncertainty parameters.

articleTitle: Mobile Based Electronic Home Appliance Remote Control and Power Consumption Monitoring Using Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Knowing which household electric appliance is consuming how much electricity is sometimes the key issue in managing domestic power consumption. In this paper, design and analysis of a low-cost and easy to implement home electric appliance controlling and energy monitoring system is proposed. The proposed system is built based on Internet of Things (IoT) equipment and protocol. This will enable the user to monitor energy consumption of connected home appliances and control them via a mobile application. The proposed system consists of two major components: IoT hardware and user interface software for that hardware. The first part is, development of an IoT prototype device that would fit inside a traditional switch board. This component contains the controlling hardware for electronic appliances, and a sensor to measure energy consumption. The prototype device has been constructed using Wi-Fi module, opto-isolated relays for communication and stability. The second part is a mobile application through which the user can control and monitor energy consumption for each home appliances. The proposed hardware and software package calculated energy consumption for a household with a reliable accuracy while it was deployed for a month. Keeping users need in mind, real-time data visualization is made available through the mobile app. The app also provides historical data summary and temporal uses comparison as well as cross device power consumption comparison.

articleTitle: The Interleaved Buck/Boost Type Voltage Balancer with Coupled-inductor in Bi-polar DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper describes the voltage balancer of interleaved buck/boost converter type with coupled inductor in DC microgrid and presents inductance deduction method of equivalent circuit model coupled inductor. Proposed voltage balancer has a role to balance voltages between positive and negative buses in bi-polar DC microgrid. The interleaved buck/boost type voltage balancer consists of two magnetic elements and it causes of bulky size of voltage balancer. To reduce volume of inductor, two-phase interleaved voltage balancer is applied. Proposed voltage balancer is tested in PSIM simulation using deduced leakage and magnetizing inductance.

articleTitle: MTPA based DTC for Permanent Magnet assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor for Electric Vehicle application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: A new maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) based direct torque control (DTC) method is proposed in this paper for a permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance motor (PMaSyRM). The central idea of the proposed control algorithm is to dynamically adjust the value of stator flux reference in accordance with the load torque. The envisaged idea enables reap more benefits from the motor drive mainly under low or no-load conditions. Analytical expression for the stator flux reference needed is presented. In addition, this paper also presents a methodology to determine the core loss component of the PMaSyRM that enables estimation of electrical losses in the motor. Firstly, performance characteristics obtainable from the PMaSyRM using the proposed MTPA based DTC is presented under different conditions. Secondly, they are compared with that obtainable from the conventional DTC method to showcase the superiority of the MTPA based DTC proposed in this paper. This is further examined by considering the Indian Drive Cycle (IDC) and an electric vehicle (EV) model. Results in terms of reduced core losses, stator copper losses and improved motor efficiency etc. are presented in support of the fusion of MTPA with DTC methods for PMaSyRM.

Author Keywords: Direct Torque Control Maximum Torque per Ampere
Permanent Magnet assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor

articleTitle: Maximum Regenerative Power Braking for Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, the maximum regenerative power braking(MRPB) method for the Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor drive is proposed. In the low-speed high-inertia motor drive system, the conventional constant-torque regenerative braking could not be ideal since the regenerative power might not be proportional to torque or stator currents. In this paper, to improve the amount of the regenerative power of the Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor drive, the model-based analysis is performed to calculate the best combination of DQ-axis current references. Also, the simple method to implement this braking method is proposed and verified by simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: A Droop Control with Deadbeat Current Strategy to Improve Response Characteristic for Three Phase Parallel AC-DC Converter in DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents a droop control with a deadbeat current strategy which overcomes the drawbacks of existing PI(Proportional-Integral) controller for three phase AC-DC converter in parallel. In case of existing the droop with PI current controller, it has sensitivity to PI controller gains as well as a high overshoot is occurred by the PI controller. However, the proposed control method shows a rapid response characteristic by minimizing the overshoot with the deadbeat current strategy. In other words, the fast dynamic response can be achieved. In this paper, input side of three phase AC-DC converter in parallel has only inductor filter to apply for deadbeat current control of the proposed method. The validity of the proposed control system is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Research of CLL Resonant DC-DC Converter with Wide Input for Battery System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, a wide input voltage dc/dc CLL resonant converter is proposed. The presented converter topology consists a Buck-boost circuit and a CLL resonant network, and therefore the Buck-Boost circuit can be used to realize wide voltage input of the CLL resonant converter. In addition, the converter adopts APWM(Asymmetric Pulse-Width Modulation) constant frequency control, which makes the implement of CLL resonant converter easy. Moreover, the employed magnetic integration and switch integration technology can greatly improve power density as well as the cost. Finally, a prototype of 30-60V dc input and 25V/10A output (250W) is designed and the validity of the theoretical analysis and the validity of the theoretical analysis and design of proposed converter is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: The Communication Requirements for Humanoid In-Robot Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In order to achieve human sensory and motor abilities, different from traditional robots, humanoid needs more sensors to receive environmental information, and more sophisticated artificial muscles to achieve similar human motion behavior. But as the number and accuracy of sensor and actuator increase, there will be a huge amount of data In this paper, we construct a humanoid network framework based on human structure and function. The bit rate of data generated by sensor and actuator in IRN will be calculatedt The results can be used as a reference for designing In-Robot Network protocols in the future.

articleTitle: A Development of Electric Tuk Tuk Conversion in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Electric Vehicle Association of Thailand (EVAT) consisting of various members in both the industrial and educational sectors related to electric vehicle, made a prototype of an electric Tuk Tuk conversion to be a guideline for SME to understand the electric Tuk Tuk (Thailand) conversion from Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicle to the electric power vehicle. This research purposed an e-Tuk Tuk conversion procedure in details to demonstrate the electric vehicles production in Thailand and its experiment. The study started on February 2lst, 2017 to December 25th, 2017. This project aims to: 1) provide the local-made electric vehicle conversion procedure; 2) establish basic requirements (specifications) for modification of electric Tuk Tuk such as power, speed, size, dimensions; and 3) provide a guideline for product development and new business model of electric Tuk Tuk and other local-made vehicles. The specification of the prototype is following; motor 5kw72V, battery LiFePo472V150Ah, maximum speed 71km./hr, maximum distant 110 km. maximum power 13kw on Dynamometer.

articleTitle: International Standard Trend of Vehicle to Grid (V2G) Communication Interface for Wireless Communication and RPT
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: ISO/IEC 1511S, titled as V2G Communication Interface specifies the communication protocol between Electric Vehicles Communication Controller (EVCC) and the Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Communication Controller (SECC). Based on power line communication (PLC), ISO/IEC 15118 Parts 1$\sim$3, were published in 2013, 2014, and 2015, respectively. ISO/IEC 1511S Part 8 and Part 1 Ed. 2 were published for wireless communication (IEEE 802.1\ln) in March 2018, April 2019, respectively. Newly revised standard of ISO/IEC 1511S Part 2 (now becomes Part 20) is currently under development for wireless communication and reverse power transfer (RPT). In this paper, important features on wireless communication and RPT, which are included in the newly added and revised standards for V2G communication interface, will be introduced. The remaining issues will be also discussed.

articleTitle: Impact analysis of deterioration and SOH estimation based on multiple regression analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: As the battery ages, the deterioration effects affect battery performance, safety and lifetime. State of health (SOH) is important to determine the lifetime of the battery [1]. To efficiently operate the battery in the electric vehicle (EV), the deterioration effect should be reflected in the parameter of equivalent circuit model (ECM). This paper quantifies the effect of parameters on degradation and proposes a SOH estimation method using multiple regression models with selected parameters. The ECM with two RC parallel circuits and an $dV/dt$ are considered to reflect the deterioration effect of the application. Multiple regression models are designed using deterioration parameters. Multiple regression analysis can also be used to quantify the effect on deterioration. The regression model verifies performance against actual capacity. Standardized regression coefficients are used to quantify the effect of parameters on deterioration. In addition, multiple regression models are designed using selected parameters. Linear regression models and multiple regression models verify performance against actual capacity.

articleTitle: A Broken Rotor Bar Fault Diagnosis Approach Based on Singular Value Decomposition and Variational Mode Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The low-amplitude side-band fault feature frequencies of broken rotor bar fault in induction motor closing to the fundamental frequency in the stator currents are easily overlapped by high-amplitude fundamental frequency. In order to solve this problem, a new fault diagnosis approach that includes singular value decomposition (SVD), variational mode decomposition (VMD) and Hilbert transform (Hilbert-VMD) is proposed. Above all, SVD efficiently filters out the fundamental component and the color noises from one phase stator current. Simultaneously, SVD also calculates the effective number of band-limited intrinsic mode functions (BLIMFs) of VMD. Next, VMD decomposes the filtered phase stator current into finite BLIMFs. Finally, Hilbert transform performs on each BLIMF and combines the Hilbert spectrum of every BLIMF. So far, the fault feature frequencies are observed easily from the processing consequences. The simulation consequences prove the excellence of the proposed approach for broken rotor bar fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: A New Demagnetization Method for Traction Transformer of Multi System Electric Locomotive
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In a multi system electric locomotive, in order to reduce the system volume, the traction winding of the traction transformer is usually used as a smoothing reactor under DC condition. In the DC power supply system, after hundreds of amps of current flow through the traction winding, the core will produce severe residual flux. When the locomotive is connected to the AC power supply network, the remanence in the core will exacerbate the magnetizing inrush current on the primary side of the transformer. In order to avoid the harm caused by residual flux, this paper proposes a new demagnetization method for locomotives. The method realizes equipment reuse, which utilizes the structure of the traction circuit itself, adding only one DC source to form the demagnetization circuit. Through the active voltage frequency conversion control, the DC voltage is continuously applied to the traction transformer in the forward and reverse directions to generate a demagnetizing current with attenuated oscillation, so that the magnetic flux is attenuated with the demagnetization current change, and finally the demagnetization effect is achieved. In this paper, the feasibility of the method is proved theoretically. Finally, the effectiveness of the demagnetization method is verified by simulation with PLECS software.

articleTitle: Tensorflow-based Long-Short term Memory Network for SOH Prediction of a Lithium-ion Cell
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Lithium-ion battery is energy storage devices that are currently used in many popular applications. It is necessary to predict the aging of lithium-ion single cell that constitutes a mass storage device to prevent failure or explosion. In order to predict SOH, a factors that affect the aging state of the battery can be selected as a characteristic parameter. The selected characteristic parameter is composed of the input of the Neural Network for predicting the SOH. Through the preliminary experiments, the variation of SOH of the lithium-ion battery according to the cycle was confirmed, and it can be divided in to the training data sets and prediction data sets. The training of the Neural Network was performed with the training data sets, and the SOH predicted through the Neural Network was compared with the actual data.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Cost Voltage Sensing Method of Three-phase Synchronous Rectifier with High-Efficiency for Automotive Alternator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Design of low-cost voltage sensing method of three-phase synchronous rectifiers with high-efficiency for automotive alternators is proposed in this paper. A new control strategy and low-cost circuitry topology are applied. There are many control methods for Power MOSFETs of synchronous rectifiers to replace the conventional rectifier diodes for the improvement of the efficiency of AC/DC rectifier. Most of those methods for such synchronous rectifiers based on operational amplifiers which are sensitive and easy interfered by electronic noise, the proposed circuitry for voltage sensing in this paper is low-cost with diodes and resistors are used to sense the positive and negative voltage of each phase for determining when to switch the synchronous rectifiers thereby emulate the operation of conventional rectifier diodes. Sensing three-phase voltage and controlling Power MOSFETs state are done by micro-controller so this method is more stable. Measurements are taken on a prototype of proposed synchronous rectification compared to a conventional diode rectification for a standard automotive alternator. The experiment shows that the efficiency of the alternator system has been raised to 95.3% in comparison with 83.5% of the conventional diode-rectified alternator at the load of 700 W.

articleTitle: Analysis of thermal characteristics of a battery module using a novel graphite material
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this study, applicability of newly developed material, carbon based graphite with enhanced thermal conductivity, as a medium to move the heat away from the cell was assessed. Thermal characteristics of a battery module consisting of pouch type cells and graphite sheets were modeled and numerically analyzed. Validation experiments were also carried out using a heating element mimicking the cells to strengthen the results from the numerical analysis. Based on simulation results and supporting experimental data, the current research demonstrated the feasibility of the new material as a part of battery pack thermal management.

articleTitle: Effective Application of Urban Renewable Energy System for Smart Energy City: Case Study of Sejong 5-1 Smart Energy City
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Based on various previous researches on zero energy building and renewable energy in Korea, we conducted a case study on application of economical rational energy technology for smart energy city implementation to Sejong 5-1 block. Through this study, it is suggested that the achievement rate of city energy independence that can be implemented in Korea in the short term at current technology and economic level is assessed.

Author Keywords: urban energy self-sufficiency rate(energy independence rate)

articleTitle: Energy management and speed profile optimization for hybrid electric trams
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Hybrid electric trams equip with additional on-board energy storage devices to improve the performance of power sources. Both of optimal energy management and velocity control are important to maximum the energy efficiency for catenary-supercapacitors hybrid trams. An optimal control model has been developed to minimize energy consumption from traction substations with supercapacitors voltage limitations. Multiple phases model transformation and solving methods are implemented to obtain the optimal voltage trajectory and speed profile simultaneously. Finally, the effect of trip time on energy consumption is assessed.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Oscillation Suppression Based on Linear ADRC Strategy in High-Speed Railways
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: With the increasing number of electric multiple units (EMUs) operating in a rail depot simultaneously, low frequency oscillation (LFO) may occur. In this paper, linear active disturbance rejection control (LADRC) is designed for the single-phase EMUs rectifier control. Moreover, Nyquist criterion is adopted to analyze the stability theoretically. Furthermore, the static and dynamic performance of the system based on LADRC is verified through the resistance mutation tests in MATLAB/Simulink comparing with traditional proportional integral (PI), nonlinear PI (NPI) and auto disturbance rejection error PI (ADRE-PI). Finally, the validity of the LFO suppression with LADRC is verified in the simulation.

articleTitle: Smart Mobility Creating Smart Space: 3D Smart Aquarium Bus
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This study aims to analyze the development of smart mobility creating smart space and expect the process of convergence evolution between smart city and vehicle. Autonomous smart vehicles make people provide time with another activities due to no driving. This study results are listed as follows. First, the functional types of inner space in smart mobility environment were divided to 3 types such as work, leisure & education, rest & health. Second, as a result of analysis about 3D Smart Aquarium Bus as smart mobility case, it had provided almost contents/services focused on leisure and education for children. The size of smart mobility was big space like bus and a number of people could enjoy good experience through various contents/services at the same time. It also had merits that could visit everywhere regardless of location, time and space. The technology of smart mobility was seriately arranged by 3D screens to maximize 3D effects of contents/services and used with 3D glasses. The development process of smart mobility had evolved like 2012(3D screen + 3D glasses: the contents of ecological environment in ocean) - 2014(3D screen + 3D glasses: the contents of ecological environment in ocean, the contents of safety education in underwater) $- 2017 \sim2018($ Only 3D screen without 3D glasses: the contents of ecological environment in ocean, the contents of safety education in underwater, The contents of renewable energy) - 2019(The creation of convergence space between building mass and bus mass for various contents/services). To sum it all up, the technology, space concept and transforming in 3D Smart Aquarium Bus was evolved by various changes of cultural and governance trends. Third, the evolution of case about leisure and education in smart mobility creating smart space was begun by contents/services based on 3D technology and changed by social issues and needs continuously. Also, the mobility space required to the further spaces through changes of various contents/services. Forth, the scale of mobility space was changed by various contents/services. Types of changing were divided to “the convergence between mobility and mobility”, “The convergence between mobility and building” and, “Self extension convergence of mobility”. In detail, the convergence between mobility and mobility was space convergence system between walls. The convergence between mobility & building and self-extension convergence of mobility were space convergence system among wall, ceiling and floor. Consequentially, the extension and evolution of smart mobility space would be made by creation of various contents/services and compactification of technologies /Infrastructures. Hereafter, these will make a various convergence system between the moved space(mobility space) and the fixed space(building space) through the evolution of sustain mass convergences, evolve the system of new creation space in smart space continually and thus, construct new creation city of future.

articleTitle: Fairness-aware Distributed Scheduling of Charging and Discharging Electric Vehicles in Dynamic Virtual Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Virtual Power Plant (VPP) is a set of distributed energy resources (DER) to provide flexible energy to the grid. Electric Vehicles (EV) are now becoming more a DER than simple load due to its discharging capability. Because of dynamic availability of EVs, the EVs can now form a Dynamic VPP (DVPP) to meet the market needs. However, because of privacy issues, it is more appropriate to form a DVPP in a distributed manner instead of centralized ones. We propose a distributed scheduling mechanism for privacy-sensitive DERs (e.g., EVs) in a DVPP, preserving fairness among DERs to promote their participations.

articleTitle: A Segmented Paper Modeling Method of Open Transformer with Three-Dimensional Wound Core by Introducing Equivalent Conductivities
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The current method to the solution of equivalent conductivity for laminated core transformer is difficult to satisfy the request of three-dimensional wound core transformer (TDWCT) due to its particular structure. In this paper, a segmented method is proposed to calculate the equivalent conductivity for TDWCT. Based on the above method, a finite-element model is set up and the simulation calculation in 3D eddy current field is performed. This paper studies the influence of the eddy current loss on the wound core at varied folding angle. It was found that there are less loss on the wound core at the folding angle are 30° and 60°, especially at 30°, However, for the other folding angle, the eddy current loss is twice as much as that of at 30°.The simulation results are useful for analyzing the influence of folding angle to wound core eddy current loss and it can provide a theoretical basis for the optimum design of TDWCT.

articleTitle: SALT-Viz: Real-Time Visualization for Large-Scale Traffic Simulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The visualization of large-scale traffic simulation is a key problem for most big cities. Moreover, it is very important to visualize results of traffic simulations for each timestep in real-time, in order to analysis urban traffic congestion status accurately. However, large-scale traffic simulation and visualization has always been considered a challenging research topic, due to the preparation difficulty of massive road networks to simulate. In this paper, we present the SALT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, a novel traffic simulator and visualizer, that can handle large-scale urban traffic simulation. It introduces the concept of dynamic detailed geometry generation using base geometric information with attributes (e.g., the number of lanes) of links in road networks. Our system can provide efficient geometry processing and real-time level-of-detail rendering of traffic simulation results. The experimental results demonstrate that our system can be successfully applied to large- scale real-world urban traffic simulation.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> SALT is the abbreviation for “Simulation for AnaLyzing urban Traffic”, which is our project code name.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of three-phase AC charging pile control system based on STM32
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Based on STM32F105VCT6 chip, this paper designs a control system for three-phase AC charging pile. Firstly, the main structure of the three-phase AC charging pile control system is proposed. Then the hardware circuit and software program of the control system are designed, including control guiding state detection circuit, three-phase voltage and current measurement circuit. The Keil μVision5 adopted in this paper is used to design control guidance circuits, state detection circuits and other software programs. The final prototype test shows that the three-phase AC charging pile control system designed in this paper can realize the correct response between the charging pile and the vehicle, and can be used in the charging field of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Multiple-Complex-Vector-Filter-Based Phase-Locked Loop Synchronization Technique for Seneorless Linear Induction Motor Drive System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The conventional synchronous reference frame phase-locked loop (SRF-PLL)-based speed estimation scheme is commonly applied in the speed-sensorless drive system. However, the inability in accurately tracking speed during the acceleration/deceleration process is a drawback of the SRF-PLL scheme. To tackle this issue, this digest proposes a new-PLL-based scheme for speed-sensorless linear induction motor (LIM) drives. The proposed scheme has two components: (1) the multiple-complex-vector-filter and the amplitude normalization are provided to reject the disturbing effect; (2) a new PLL is used for enforcing the estimated speed information. Simulations are implemented to demonstrate the speed scheme in LIM speed-sensorless systems.

articleTitle: Design a High-Speed Segmental Stator Type 4/3 SRM for Blender Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents a design of a high-speed segmental stator type 4/3 switched reluctance motor (SRM) for blender application. The stator of the proposed motor consists of two independent segmental U-cores, and each U-core has two stator poles, there are no steel connections between two cores. Two phases of the proposed motor are operated independently, and there are no reversal or mutual flux. The rotor has three poles with a stepper air gap. The stepped air gap is applied to the rotor shape to overcome the torque dead-zone and release self-starting ability. The rotor can rotate in one direction only; this motor type is suitable for unidirectional rotation application. Phase excitation forms a short flux path in U-core; the flux travels in the exciting phase only. The flux path in the proposed motor is shorter compared with a convention SRM that results in reducing the magnetomotive force to produce the same output torque. The design was verified by finite element analysis. The operation principle and characteristic of the proposed motor will be presented in detail. The average torque of the proposed motor is 60% higher compared with that of a 4/2 SRM.

articleTitle: Implement of High Efficiency Achievement Algorithm of LDC for xEV based on GaN HEMT
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents a method to improve the efficiency of LDC for xEV. First, implement of high efficiency hardware using GaN HEMT, which is the next generation semiconductor, and propose and apply an active parallel control algorithm to improve light and medium load efficiency. The proposed LDC control method is explained in detail by operation mode, and a 1.2kW class prototype LDC is implemented to verify the superiority of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Optimal Design and Analysis of Interior Permanent Magnet Motor for High-thrust Drone
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The attention in the use of permanent magnet motors has highlighted the importance of IPM (Interior Permanent Magnet) structure, high power and high efficiency rotor design. This paper puts forward the optimal design method for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and interior permanent magnet motors for drones that require high thrust of high rotational speed. The size of the motor stator was fixed to minimize the number of variables in the analysis and only the rotor shape was modified to compare torque and output power.

articleTitle: E-Truck Conversion with a Bi-Directional OBC
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Exhaust gas, especially carbon dioxide, from conventional vehicles is thought to be a major cause of climate change. Some countries around the world are even trying to restrict the operation of diesel vehicles in order to alleviate severe pollution issues. In particular, in the case of aged diesel trucks, Korean government has proposed a disposal plan. However, disposal of diesel trucks can be significant financial losses. To reduce these losses, the some automobile experts are trying to establish standardized EV conversion procedures of diesel vehicles. In this paper, a 1 ton diesel truck is electrified along with a bi-directional OBC which could be used to support the vehicle to grid (V2G) function later on. Based on the experience from the current study, suggestions for the standardized CAN protocol for important battery parameters are discussed to open the better and easier re-use of retired battery packs as energy storage systems.

articleTitle: Coordinated Vehicle-to-Grid Control to Participate in Secondary Frequency Regulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Since a plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs) fleet can behave like a storage system and earn extra money by participating in secondary frequency regulation (SFR), a proper method that coordinates all the PEVs within this fleet is required. This paper introduces a coordinated vehicle-to-grid (V2G) control method to enable a PEV aggregator to participate in SFR, where the aggregator only needs to broadcast a simple signal and the PEVs decide their own control commands by solving an optimization problem iteratively through peer-to-peer communication. Compared with centralized method, the computational and communicational burden are remarkably alleviated by the proposed method. The objective to maintain the availability of PEVs during participating in SFR is also carefully considered. The effectiveness of proposed method is demonstrated via numerical simulations of a V2G fleet.

articleTitle: Research on Harmonic Resonance in Traction Power-Supply System Containing a Thyristor-Based Neutral Section System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Harmonic resonance phenomenon was found in traction power-supply system (TPSS) after an automatic thyristor-based neutral section system (ATNSS) has been installed in Shenshuo Railway, China. Harmonic resonance usually occurs in the coupling system between the TPSS and the trains. However, no previous researches show the participation of the ATNSS. In this paper, with the concentration of the harmonic resonance of the coupling system, a solution is proposed to get the impedance vs frequency characteristics of TPSS. The influences of thyristor voltage-balancing parameters have been investigated based on MATLAB/Simulink, and the study of their impact on the power network voltage was carried out. The results show that adjusting dynamic voltage-balancing capacitors appropriately could effectively suppress the high-frequency resonant overvoltage of TPSS.

articleTitle: Passivity-based Decoupling Control of Single-phase LCL-type VSR in Train for Harmonics Suppression in Railway System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: LCL-type filter was widely put forward for suppressing high-frequency harmonic current of grid-connected voltage source converter (VSC) systems. In this paper, single-phase LCL-type voltage source rectifier (VSR) of traction drive system is utilized for harmonics resonance suppression, a passivity-based decoupling control (PBDC) scheme is presented to improve performance of single-phase LCL-type VSR,. The passivity-based controller adopt by the system can make it global stability. Furthermore, when the controller is constructed in synchronously rotating frame, the active current and reactive current can be controlled without coupling. Firstly, derived dynamical modeling and Euler-Lagrange (EL) modeling of single-phase LCL-type VSR system are established in synchronously rotating frame. Second, fast dynamic response can be achieved with damp injecting method. Third, a capacitor voltage loop is added in the controller, which contribute to achieve resonance damping. Therefore, a passivity-based decoupling controller is meticulously designed. Finally, simulation and experiments is carried out, the results prove the validity of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Energy Resources Management Strategy for Agricultural Range Extended Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this study, the energy resource management strategy applied to the agricultural Range-extended Electric Vehicles (Re-EVs) is proposed. The strategy alerts users based on their power consumption trends and preventing the vehicle from being fully discharged. A strategy of making the most of fuel resources by determining when to operate the generator is introduced. This strategy can be applied to other types of ReEVs with different battery capacity and generator output.

articleTitle: Active Design Aided Deep Learning for Reliability of DC-Link Capacitor in Traction Drive System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In order to solve the reliability problem of DC-link capacitor, a capacitor active design method based on deep learning is proposed. Staring from the introduction of two test case, the electrical parameters of film capacitor are collected and the lifetime expectancy of the capacitors is solved. A deep learning network model is established through the Deep Neural Network. The model can quickly and accurately map the performance parameters of capacitors to the volume, cost and lifetime expectancy of the selected dc-link capacitors, and realize the selection and design of the DC-link film capacitor in the traction drive system.

articleTitle: A New Saliency-Based Sensorless Method For Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In high-frequency square-wave injection sensorless methods, the amplitude of the carrier current which is used for rotor position estimation depends to the injection voltage amplitude and reversely to the injection frequency. Increasing the injection signal amplitude will increase the acoustic noise level and high-frequency losses. In this paper, a new pulsating semi-impulse signal injection method by the technique of measuring the high-frequency current is proposed for the sensorless control of interior permanent magnet synchronous motors (IPMSM). In the proposed method not only the benefits of the square-wave methods can be achieved but also the unwilling issues caused by high-frequency injection such as acoustic noise and power losses will be reduced. Hence, the scope of the sensorless drive application will be developed by aiding the proposed method especially for some applications which are sensitive to the audible noise such as a home appliances. The proposed method has been tested by simulation results and implementing experimental tests.

articleTitle: Coordinate Estimation Scheme for Differential Mobile Robots Using Rotary Encoder
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Real-time coordinate estimation for a mobile robot is a crucial task for its control. In this paper we propose three coordinate estimation schemes for differential mobile robots using a pair of rotary encoders. Rotary encoders installed on the differential axis. Firstly, we recover the yaw angle and absolute velocities for each wheels. Then, calculate the velocity vectors for each wheels and integrate them to estimate coordinates. The schemes is numerically simulated on Matlab. For this we construct smooth trajectories for each wheel using Bezier polynomials. We calculate Bezier time instances that divides the curve into equal segments. This is done by solving first-order nonlinear ODE of Bezier time with respect to the natural parameter of the curves. We run our scheme on these time instances and evaluate its estimation error. The coordinate estimation schemes are implemented and experimented on a ARM computer.

articleTitle: Technical Evaluation of Utility-Interactive Photovoltaic Power Generation System with Energy Storage based on the Experimental Setup
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: There is harmful air-pollution which mainly caused by raw-coal firing for heating purpose in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. Although dominantly utilization of electricity-powered warmers is good solution for this issue as same as highly developed countries, local power system currently in use has already been in over-stress during sundown interval as most of residents actively use home electric appliances. Therefore, the authors intend to lessen the polluted-ingredients of urban area air by using latest technology development. The distributed-generation system with renewable source and battery storage can be the bright solution. Within this paper, an appropriate configuration of the utility-interactive photovoltaic (PV) power generation system with energy storage (ES) for locals, and its operation principle are discussed. Subsequently, an adapted operation algorithm which gives an economical advantage, and contributes for grid impact is applied. Then, the experimental setup to verify the feasibility of recommended structure and operation algorithm is implemented. Development of the PV power generation system with ES will lead to a reduction in peak power usage, and lessened amount of CO2 emissions is expected to be resulted.

articleTitle: AC-DC Multi-port Traction Power Supply System with Power Electronic Transformer
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, an AC-DC multi-port traction power supply system with power electronic transformer is put forward. Based on this structure, the system control method is proposed to realize energy optimization and system stabilization. The system control method is proposed to divide the system state and utilize DC bus voltage information, aiming at achieving optimal energy utilization and system stability. The system consists of PV (photovoltaic) source DC system, wind energy communication system, energy storage module, regenerative braking module, DC micro-grid power supply module and local load, which can run in grid or island mode. The system is divided into five working modes, which are the main control DC bus voltage of PV source DC system under balanced state, the main control of island operation energy storage module, the main control of regenerative braking module, and the main control and communication of regenerative braking module in grid mode. The control methods of the PV interface converter, the grid side interface converter and the energy storage interface converter are respectively given. The simulation and the test results proof the usefulness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Dynamic Simulation of a Large Power System with High-Capacity Photovoltaic Systems Able to Control Reactive Power
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Relatively small-capacity distributed or clustered photovoltaic (PV) systems change dynamic behaviors of the feeder despite their small capacity. Moreover, modern distributed generation (DG) inverters can control reactive power (i.e., Volt/Var control and management). To connect higher capacity PV systems (i.e., above 50 percent of the total feeder rating) able to control reactive power, various steady-state, transient behaviors, and short-circuit currents affected by the PV systems should be examined in an actual power grid. Thus, the objective of this study is to examine feeder dynamics affected by such a high-capacity PV system able to control reactive power. For this purpose, this study initially models an actual large power grid with thousands of nodes in DIgSILENT, adds high-capacity PV systems (i.e., 50 percent of the feeder rating) with a Volt/Var droop controller to the grid, and generates switching events (i.e.., the circuit breaker on/of) and faults. The Volt/Var control of a high-capacity PV system could mitigate an increase in overvoltage and affect the post-fault voltage because of controlling reactive power. The case study results can be used for the smooth integration of high-capacity DG systems to the grid.

articleTitle: Resonance Circuit Design for Current Ripple Reduction of Semi-Bridgeless Rectifier Applying PDM Control in IPT System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, a resonant network design is proposed to minimize the primary side effects that appear when pulse density modulation (PDM) control is applied to semi-bridgeless rectifier in secondary side of an inductive power transfer (IPT) system. In order to solve the problem that current in the secondary side is increased when PDM control is applied, current ripple is reduced by minimizing primary side influence by increasing secondary side receiving inductance. Furthermore, a method to obtain appropriate design conditions is proposed and the effect of the primary side according to the application of the method is analyzed through simulation.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control with Dead-Beat Structure Based Field Weakening Sterategy for SPMSM
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper deals with the implementation of predictive control in the field weakening region for SPMSM. The structure of the predictive controller is dead-beat which is not used for field weakening region for SPMSM yet. In the conventional flux weakening algorithm, an additional PI regulator or low pass filter is needed to adjust the d-axis current reference. Therefore, a sophisticated gain tuning for this regulator in the presence of two PI regulators for current loops is a critical issue. In addition, this type of controller represents a low bandwidth for high-speed drive systems. So to overcome the mentioned problems a dead beat controller is proposed for flux weakening region of this type of motors. For deliberation of this controller, its performance is compared with PI and FCS-MPC controllers. Advantages of the controller in the field weakening region compared to two other controllers is presented. Simulation result shows the superiority of the controller.

articleTitle: Extraction of Parasagittal Meningioma Tumor using Skull Stripping Method and Multilevel Thresholding
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Tumors are abnormal growth of tissues in the body, which can be benign or malignant. Meningioma is a type of tumor in the Brain that emerges from the layer of tissue known as meninges and surrounds the brain and the spine inside the skull. Parasagittal meningioma's appears along the superior sagittal sinus and are attached to the dura that run between the left and the right sides of the brain. Growth rates for parasagittal meningioma are slow and might take years before it gets detected. Due to its location and the possibility of injuring the sinus, surgery of parasagittal meningioma tumors are complicated and require early detection. In this paper we propose a simple algorithm to extract parasagittal meningioma tumor from magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography scanned images using skull stripping and multilevel thresholding method. The use of machine learning techniques in diagnosing or analyzing biomedical issues are trending and rapidly growing due its ease, accuracy, cost effectiveness and less time requirement in detecting a disease from MRI or CT scanned images as well as other form of images gained from medical imaging technologies. The algorithm has been tested on 150 DICOM images and the result showed the accuracy of the algorithm and its efficiency in correctly detecting parasagittal meningioma tumors in the brain.

articleTitle: Rotor Eddy Current Loss Research and Design Factors Analysis on Thermal Performance for a High-Speed Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, rotor eddy current loss and thermal performance analysis for a 150 kW, 17000 rpm highspeed permanent magnet synchronous machine are presented. Firstly, machine structure is introduced with prototype manufactured. Then, machine rotor eddy current loss is comprehensively investigated by Finite element method. The influences from machine design parameters on eddy current loss are studied. Moreover, composite rotor structure with the combinations of different rotor sleeve and shielding sets are proposed and studied for rotor loss reduction. Machine thermal performance is also researched by Computational Fluid Dynamics with the factors effecting machine temperature analyzed and discussed

articleTitle: Research on Voltage SPM Modulation Strategy of 3LNPC-CI when DC port fault
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Aiming at the multi-module three-level neutral point clamp cascaded inverter (3LNPC-CI) when suffers from DC port fault, a sequence pulse modulation (SPM) is proposed, to deal with the problem of unbalanced capacitor voltage not only inner the module but also between modules. What’s more, the module level of each module should remain unchanged. The proposed modulation has the advantage of simple calculation and control stability. Experiment has been done to verify the SPM.

Author Keywords: three-level neutral point clamp cascaded rectifier

articleTitle: A Nonlinear Three-dimensional Flux Linkage Modeling Method for Axial Flux Coil Assisted Stator Excitation BLDCM Based on Fourier Series
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, an axial flux coil assisted stator excitation BLDCM (CASEM) is designed. Because of the high magnetic saturation and strong coupling, the mathematical model of the motor has strong nonlinearity, and it is difficult to establish an accurate flux linkage model. Therefore, a three-dimensional flux linkage modeling method based on Fourier series is proposed in this paper, which considers multi-phase coupling and non-linear problems. Finally, a simulation model and an experimental platform are established to verify the correctness and effectiveness of the modeling method, which lays a foundation for further research on motor control to reduce torque ripple.

articleTitle: An Improved Finite-Set Model Predictive Current Control for 3L-HANPC Inverter Fed PMSM Drives
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper proposes an advanced finite-set model predictive current control (FS-MPCC) for permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drives fed by three-level hybrid active neutral point clamped (3L-HANPC) inverter. The 3L-HANPC which is state of the art in multilevel topology provides outstanding performances in terms of system efficiency and thermal behavior of switching devices in bi-directional power delivery. Computational burden is a major hurdle for practical implementation of FS-MPCC of motor drive. To reduce the huge computation and calculation time, the optimal section is determined thus the number of voltage vectors is selected and the calculation time for cost function can be reduced. Simulation results confirm that the computation burden could be reduced while dynamic performance is comparable with the conventional all voltage-vectors based FS-MPCC.

articleTitle: Sensor Fault Diagnosis and Fault-Tolerant Approach Based on State Observer for Single-Phase Cascaded H-Bridge Rectifiers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents a fast and reliable fault diagnosis and fault-tolerant approach for grid current and dc-link voltages sensor faults in the single-phase cascaded H-bridge rectifiers (SPCHBR). Firstly, a state observer with the mixed logic dynamic (MLD) model is established for obtaining the observed sensor signals and system residuals. And then normalized residuals are generated to diagnose and isolate single or multiple sensor faults online by comparing different residuals with thresholds. Moreover, fault-tolerant control is realized by redesigning the observer gain and substituting the observed values for the measured values. The proposed approach can accomplish the accurate location of the faulty sensors and system reconfiguration within half of the current fundamental period. The effectiveness and availability of the proposed approach has been verified by MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: The Case Study of Smart Home in LH
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: LH made ‘Smart Home Action Plan’ to develop service element technologies and platform of Smart Home, and is carrying out 32 practical tasks. LH plans to develop and distribute a universal smart home service model that can be extended to 1 million rental housing units. Before that, it is promoting a pilot project for 5,000 public rental housing in Siheung-Eungye. As LH’s inventory of rental housing is expected to increase to more than 2 million units by the next 10 years, it is required how to focus on housing welfare, safety and security services for vulnerable people through smart home technology, and to develop and spread smart home services based on universal housing welfare.

articleTitle: 2-Shifts AMT Nonlinear Vibration Analysis of Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Installing a 2-shifts or 3-shifts gearbox on electric vehicle is one way to enhance the vehicle’s onboard energy utility. However, the existence of the electric vehicle transmission system may cause torque fluctuation. In order to ensure the smoothness during the operation, a novel nonlinear dynamic model of 2-shifts helical gear AMT works in shift I status is established. This model has abilities to investigate the vibration coupling mechanism between the meshed gears. The results show proposed model can accurately reflect the coupling relationship of the system.

articleTitle: The Newton-Raphson method for optimization of distributed generation resources
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method for the optimization of distributed generation (DG) through power flow studies. A variety of reasons (e.g., greenhouse gas emissions, the depletion of fossil fuels, or the environmental impact of nuclear power) increase the need for DG. So, the analysis of the location and capacity of DG has become necessary and its optimization is required. For the optimization of DG, we initially implement a Newton-Raphson algorithm using MATLAB. An optimization method of power flow interpreted by the Newton-Raphson algorithm is presented.

articleTitle: Air-Gap Magnetic Field Analysis of Dual-Stator Brushless Doubly-Fed Generator Based on Analytic Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel dual-stator brushless doubly-fed generator (DSBDFG) with cage-barrier rotor structure for wind power generation. Due to DSBDFG structure and magnetic field complexity, this paper proposes groove-by-groove method to analyze equivalent current density of control winding and power winding. Meanwhile, divided layers model of DSBDFG is built. Magnetic vector potential is regarded as variables to obtain two-dimensional solution of control winding and power winding excitation. On this basis, electromagnetic parameters of DSBDFG are analyzed, which is verified by finite element method and experiment. Through analysis of the results, it demonstrates the validity and rationality of analytical method.

articleTitle: Assessment of Ubiquitous Energy from Cow Urine
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents the impact of a new electricity production source: cow urine. The Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) ratio analysis and its implications applying waste management through recycling process of cow urine are also empirically analyzed in this paper. The proposed model works like a conventional battery system; however, no additional electricity is needed in this system as conventional batteries. Only the continued replacement of a fresh batch of cow urine is required for the system to generate electricity as a ubiquitous energy source. Load factor (λ) of the proposed system is 58.33%, which showed the potentiality of providing electricity in the remote areas through the proposed electricity source. Finally, the prototype result of the proposed system is shown that it is possible to lit up a household with LED lights for 6-8 hours/day using 18 liters of cow urine.

articleTitle: Analysis of Voltage Oscillation of Shipboards MVDC Systems with VSG Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Offshore shipboards have been one of the major transportation schemes, of which medium voltage dc shipboard integrated power systems is the main constitutes of the shipboards. DC voltage is prone to oscillation even instability due to dynamic interaction between different power converters or between converter and DC network. To explore stability of DC voltage of SIPS, the impedance model is proposed. A virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control strategy is proposed to improve inertia, damping performance of DC shipboard integrated power systems (SIPS) to guarantee stable and secure operation of the system. The principle of VSG control strategy with damping oscillation of DC voltage of SIPS is analyzed. Simulations are developed to validate the proposed conceives. Finally, the conclusion is drawn.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis and Calculation of Double Stator Brushless Doubly-Fed Generator for Wind Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Compared with common generators, brushless doubly-fed generator (BDFG) has the disadvantages of lower power density and efficiency. In order to overcome these defects, a double stator brushless doubly-fed generator (DSBDFG) has been proposed. However, due to its complicated mechanical structure, the heat dissipation is difficult, resulting in the problem of excessive local temperature rise easily. Therefore, in order to avoid the risk of overheating, accurate calculation of temperature rise for DSBDFG is crucial. In response to this question, a novel equivalent thermal network model is proposed. The correctness of the proposed thermal model is verified by FEM calculation results.

articleTitle: Neural network based SOC estimation during cycle aging using voltage and internal resistance
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The state of charge(SOC) estimation of a Lithium-ion battery is critical and fundamental in managing and using it safely and optimally. The SOC estimation often overlooks the effects of aging and cycling of the battery. This paper presents a model free estimation method based on the Neural network algorithm using the terminal voltage and the internal resistance instead of the capacity. The terminal voltage plays a role in the SOC estimation of each cycle and the internal resistance adapts it according to the cycle aging effect. After the training of the network for a few intermittent cycle numbers, the SOC estimation error with different cycle numbers for testing results in less than 3 percent. This method can be used in the EV battery applications in which the model parameters are not easy to obtain.

articleTitle: Road Load Simulation Algorithms Evaluation Using A Motor-in-the-loop Test Bench
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: resent research evaluates three typical road load algorithms, like PI algorithm (PIA), feed forward algorithm (FFA) and inverse model algorithm (IMA), for electric powertrain testing. Models of vehicle, driver and test bench are established in MATLAB/Simulink environment, which has structural consistency with real motor-in-the-loop test bench. A novel vehicle state observation is used to reflect the effect of road loading and inertia emulation. To evaluate road load simulation, each algorithm is validated in off-line simulation and HIL testing. The results show FFA and IMA have advantageous in speed control precision, torque responds and state point tracking.

articleTitle: Emergency Control of Electric Vehicle Charging Station Based on Second Order Power Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: An emergency control strategy of electric vehicle charging station (EVCS) is proposed to avoid transmission line overload, where the second order power sensitivity is considered. In this paper, EVCSs are considered to be flexible load, which can be controlled for enhancing the system security. Compared to the traditional sensitivity method, the second order sensitivity can capture the nonlinearity better, especially when the system is with heavy load. Case studies show that the proposed method can provide more effective results, when the system nonlinearity is strong.

articleTitle: Analysis of Equivalent Circuit Model Parameter Change Tendency Based on C-rate of NMC Battery
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, the tendency of the battery equivalent circuit model parameters which changes according to the C-rate is analyzed, and based on this, a method to estimate the state of the battery without using all lookup tables (LUT) of the corresponding parameters is suggested. The proposed method is effective in reducing the computational burden of battery management system (BMS) by cutting the number of LUTs according to various C-rate. The validity of this study is verified by comparing the simulated terminal voltage composed of the parameters to the reference terminal voltage. For the experimental verification, Nickel Manganese Cobalt (NMC) type battery cell is used.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Filter for Wideband Frequency Harmonics Eliminating
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: A hybrid filter (HF) which contains a passive part and an active part is proposed to eliminate wideband frequency harmonics ranging from low-order harmonics to high-order harmonics in high-voltage occasions. To decrease the capacity of the active part, the active part is connected in series with the fundamental parallel resonance circuit and, thus, greatly reduces its voltage ratings of active part. The passive part made up of fundamental parallel resonance circuit (PRC1), resistance R1, 3rd harmonic parallel resonance circuit (PRC3) and 5th harmonic parallel resonance circuit (PRC5) connected in series, acts as a filter which filtering the high-order harmonics. Furthermore, the configuration of PRC3 and PRC5 can block 3rd and 5th harmonic currents flowing through itself, which ensures a better compensation for the low-order harmonic currents. The simulation and a small-scale protype are built. The simulation and experimental results verify that the proposed HF has a better compensation effect to the wideband frequency harmonics.

articleTitle: Control Algorithm Integrated FEM Based Starting Capability Analysis of Induction Motor and PMSM for Electrical Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: With the development of technology, different types’ motors and control strategies are used in motor system for electric vehicle. Their starting capability are different according by motor types, control strategies and operating temperature. As a comparison, we analyze the starting capability of PMSM and IM in this paper. A 2D FEM integrated with control algorithm is applied to simulate the different working conditions for these motors, the starting capability with different control strategies are compared. Experiment results are consistent with the simulation results. The results show that the two motors have different maximum torque under the same protection current, and the design method described in this paper can be used as a reference for the design of electric vehicle drive motor.
